_about: PLACEHOLDER lines for Harrow Landing (M3-4), re-toned 2026-10-08 to the grim-world, loud-heroes tone (docs/tone_guide.md, Writer pass). Still PLACEHOLDER: the formal dialogue sign-off is M6-2 and needs Ross. Locked: the bridge lamp examine line (harrow_ex_bridge_lamp) is the story bible's own wording. Townsfolk speak as crowd_* ids (plain box). Lines change by story beat through the 'variants' of each NPC in data/world/placements.json (b1_night, b2_otis_joined, b3_home_again). Rule of thumb: B1 is quiet and short, B2 gets louder, B3 is loud, because the town is getting its voice back. Kasp's memos (story bible, Kasp) are used as examine text on the notice board and the checkpoint poster. The dark window is the one above the store (Ross's tone call D2 B: about half of Lamp Square is dark and a few windows relight).

harrow_bettor_b1.speaker: crowd_bettor
harrow_bettor_b1.text: Two rations says the Zeroes crack by morning. Odds are always good on people cracking.

harrow_bettor_b1.speaker: crowd_bettor
harrow_bettor_b1.text: Care to bet, courier? ...No? Smart. I'd lose it.

harrow_bettor_b2.speaker: crowd_bettor
harrow_bettor_b2.text: A courier and a bear. Kasp's whole crew. ...I have to REWRITE THE BOARD.

harrow_bettor_b2.speaker: crowd_bettor
harrow_bettor_b2.text: Chalk costs a ration a stick. Worth every one.

harrow_bettor_b3.speaker: crowd_bettor
harrow_bettor_b3.text: Paying out. All of it. Everybody bet on you and NOBODY TOLD ME.

harrow_bettor_b3.speaker: crowd_bettor
harrow_bettor_b3.text: I'm fine. Very fine. Here's your... nothing. ...Go away before I start smiling in public.

harrow_neighbor_b1.speaker: crowd_neighbor
harrow_neighbor_b1.text: Your lamp's lit again, Red. I set my clock by it. ...Mine went out in the spring. Couldn't see the point.

harrow_neighbor_b2.speaker: crowd_neighbor
harrow_neighbor_b2.text: Heard the docks got loud. I opened my window to listen. First time in a year.

harrow_neighbor_b3.speaker: crowd_neighbor
harrow_neighbor_b3.text: Look up. More windows lit than an hour ago. ...I counted twice.

harrow_snack_b1.speaker: crowd_snack_seller
harrow_snack_b1.text: Protein bars. Real ones, not quota bars. Half price if you're not wearing headphones. Don't ask whose truck.

harrow_snack_b2.speaker: crowd_snack_seller
harrow_snack_b2.text: Sold out. The Signals bought the lot, then ticketed me for the wrapper noise.

harrow_gate_shut.speaker: crowd_dockhand
harrow_gate_shut.text: Docks are shut, Red. Signals business. ...You'd need a claim slip.

harrow_gate_open.speaker: crowd_dockhand
harrow_gate_open.text: That's a claim slip. Go on down. ...I didn't see you. I haven't seen anything in years.

harrow_legend_square.speaker: crowd_barfly
harrow_legend_square.text: ...and Red flattened FIFTY troopers! With a LAMP!

harrow_legend_square.speaker: narrator
harrow_legend_square.text: (Red holds up three fingers. Then two more. Then flexes.)

harrow_ex_lamp_post.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_lamp_post.text: The public lamp post. Tall and crooked, one of the last bulbs on the square. It hums a little song. Nobody's ticketed it yet.

harrow_ex_bets_b1.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bets_b1.text: THE BETS. KASP VS WATCH ZERO: WHO CRACKS FIRST. Stakes are in rations now. Most of the odds are crossed out.

harrow_ex_bets_b2.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bets_b2.text: The board has been rewritten in a hurry. COURIER AND A BEAR: 1 to 1. Someone underlined it twice.

harrow_ex_bets_b3.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bets_b3.text: PAID OUT, says the board, in angry capitals. Below it, smaller: NEXT BET: SOMETHING BIGGER.

harrow_ex_notice.speaker: sign
harrow_ex_notice.text: QUIET HOURS SAVE LIVES. Signals Corps thanks you for your silence.

harrow_ex_notice.speaker: sign
harrow_ex_notice.text: MEMO. Windows lit after Quiet Hours will be assumed to be signaling. Signaling is treason. Have a restful night. - K.

harrow_ex_notice.speaker: sign
harrow_ex_notice.text: (Someone has chalked a small lamp over Kasp's face. Someone else tried to scrub it off. The lamp is winning.)

harrow_window_dark.speaker: narrator
harrow_window_dark.text: A dark window above the store. The lamp on the sill is empty and cold. Somebody still keeps the glass clean.

harrow_window_done.speaker: narrator
harrow_window_done.text: The window glows. Somebody inside is humming, very softly.

harrow_window_light.speaker: narrator
harrow_window_light.text: Red pours in the lamp oil, taps the glass twice, and lights the lamp.

harrow_window_light.speaker: narrator
harrow_window_light.text: The window above the store glows. One more lit window on Lamp Square. Across the way, a curtain moves.

harrow_window_reward.speaker: narrator
harrow_window_reward.text: Something shiny has appeared on the sill. Payment, apparently. Nobody saw who left it.

harrow_dock_1.speaker: kasp
harrow_dock_1.text: Quiet Hours save lives, dockhands. Ticket for you. Ticket for you. Ticket for the crate.

harrow_dock_1.speaker: crowd_grunt
harrow_dock_1.text: Sarge, that crate is just... standing there.

harrow_dock_1.speaker: kasp
harrow_dock_1.text: STANDING IS A NOISE. Write it up.

harrow_dock_2.speaker: otis
harrow_dock_2.text: Sorry to interrupt, friend. Those are my dockhands. Their ration cards can't take another ticket.

harrow_dock_2.speaker: kasp
harrow_dock_2.text: Dockmaster. You are obstructing a Signals action. Grunts, ticket him. In triplicate.

harrow_dock_2.speaker: otis
harrow_dock_2.text: Mm. She's already swinging. I'll have to catch up.

harrow_dock_3.speaker: kasp
harrow_dock_3.text: This is not over. I am circling back. Via the checkpoint. With forms. A great many forms.

harrow_dock_3.speaker: otis
harrow_dock_3.text: Well. That was loud. ...It felt good. Mind if I tag along, friend?

harrow_dock_3.speaker: otis
harrow_dock_3.text: Your crate's in my office, slip or no slip. And my hammer's been bored for years.

harrow_dock_kasp_idle.speaker: crowd_grunt
harrow_dock_kasp_idle.text: Not now. Forty tickets before shift ends. Then lunch.

harrow_dock_hand_a_b1.speaker: crowd_dockhand
harrow_dock_hand_a_b1.text: Please don't make noise. Please don't make noise...

harrow_dock_hand_a_b2.speaker: crowd_dockhand
harrow_dock_hand_a_b2.text: You hit him. You hit a Sergeant. ...I forgot that was allowed.

harrow_dock_hand_a_b3.speaker: crowd_dockhand
harrow_dock_hand_a_b3.text: Dockhands are standing up straighter this week. Nobody says why. We all know.

harrow_dock_hand_b_b1.speaker: crowd_dockhand_b
harrow_dock_hand_b_b1.text: They wrote me a ticket for 'standing near a crate'.

harrow_dock_hand_b_b2.speaker: crowd_dockhand_b
harrow_dock_hand_b_b2.text: I'm framing my ticket. 'Standing near a crate.' Best day of my career.

harrow_dock_hand_b_b3.speaker: crowd_dockhand_b
harrow_dock_hand_b_b3.text: We reenact the fight on lunch break. I'm the crate. It's a lot of pressure.

harrow_pell_b1.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_pell_b1.text: Shh. Trying to look like a crate. ...Crates get ticketed too. I've seen it.

harrow_pell_b2.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_pell_b2.text: Thanks, Red. If the courier board has a paperwork job, take it. I know paperwork. Painfully.

harrow_pell_b3.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_pell_b3.text: Reenact the fight? Sure. I'll be Kasp. 'Ticket for you. Ticket for you.' ...Everyone laughs. It's a miracle.

harrow_pell_form.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_pell_form.text: An Appeal Form! Signals hands out the tickets, but never mention the forms. You have to know somebody.

harrow_pell_form.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_pell_form.text: Drop it in the APPEALS slot at the checkpoint booth. In triplicate. Well, once. It's a start.

harrow_pell_go.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_pell_go.text: Booth slot, checkpoint. Don't fold it. They hate it when you fold it.

harrow_pell_done.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_pell_done.text: Filed. They said my appeal is important to them. ...Nobody's said that to me in years.

harrow_ex_crane.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_crane.text: A crane. It's been 'out of service' for as long as anyone remembers. A sign says so, repeatedly.

harrow_ex_tide.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_tide.text: A tide board, chalked by hand. HIGH: later. LOW: earlier. WET: always.

harrow_ex_roster_window.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_roster_window.text: A window into Otis's office. A roster board hangs on the wall, every name in neat chalk.

harrow_cp_ticket.speaker: crowd_grunt
harrow_cp_ticket.text: That's a wind chime. Wind chimes are noise. That's a noise ticket.

harrow_cp_ticket.speaker: crowd_grunt
harrow_cp_ticket.text: Forty credits, off the ration card. Next.

harrow_cp_grunt.speaker: crowd_grunt
harrow_cp_grunt.text: Road's closed. Signals business. Move along.

harrow_cp_otis_1.speaker: otis
harrow_cp_otis_1.text: Barrier's stuck, friend. Let me see... there.

harrow_cp_otis_1.speaker: narrator
harrow_cp_otis_1.text: (Otis lifts the boom barrier and props it open. Nobody in line breathes.)

harrow_cp_fan_a_b1.speaker: crowd_chime_fan
harrow_cp_fan_a_b1.text: They ticketed my chime. Forty credits, off the ration card. ...It was my dad's. It barely even rings.

harrow_cp_fan_a_b2.speaker: crowd_chime_fan
harrow_cp_fan_a_b2.text: They left. Radioed up the tower. ...Can I hang my chime up? ...I'm hanging my chime up.

harrow_cp_fan_a_b3.speaker: crowd_chime_fan
harrow_cp_fan_a_b3.text: Chime's back up. Hear it? ...No wind tonight. Doesn't matter. It's up, and it's mine.

harrow_cp_fan_b_b1.speaker: crowd_grumbler
harrow_cp_fan_b_b1.text: Forty credits for a ding. ...I'd have paid forty to hear it.

harrow_cp_fan_b_b2.speaker: crowd_grumbler
harrow_cp_fan_b_b2.text: Didn't even say goodbye. Rude. I'd have said goodbye.

harrow_cp_fan_b_b3.speaker: crowd_grumbler
harrow_cp_fan_b_b3.text: I hung up my chimes. All twelve. The neighbors are complaining. ...I've missed complaints.

harrow_cp_fan_c_b1.speaker: crowd_chime_kid
harrow_cp_fan_c_b1.text: Shh. I'm not humming. ...I'm just breathing in tune.

harrow_cp_fan_c_b2.speaker: crowd_chime_kid
harrow_cp_fan_c_b2.text: They're GONE. ...Can I hum now? I'm humming now! I'M HUMMING!

harrow_cp_fan_c_b3.speaker: crowd_chime_kid
harrow_cp_fan_c_b3.text: Teaching my little sister a lane-song. Out loud. In the street. She's awful. I love it.

harrow_ex_poster.speaker: sign
harrow_ex_poster.text: MEMO. Effective tonight, grief is a noise. Mourners will be ticketed at the standard rate. Quietly. - Sgt. Kasp

harrow_appeal_empty.speaker: sign
harrow_appeal_empty.text: APPEALS. Please insert an appeal. Your appeal is important to us.

harrow_appeal_drop.speaker: narrator
harrow_appeal_drop.text: Red slides the form into the APPEALS slot.

harrow_appeal_drop.speaker: sign
harrow_appeal_drop.text: Your appeal is important to us. Please hold. Forever.

harrow_appeal_drop.speaker: crowd_pell
harrow_appeal_drop.text: It's in! I saw it go in! From the arch!

harrow_appeal_paid.speaker: narrator
harrow_appeal_paid.text: Pell hurries over, grinning like he got away with something, and hands Red a handful of credits and two spare forms.

harrow_appeal_done.speaker: sign
harrow_appeal_done.text: Your appeal has been appealed. Thank you for your patience. (It was not needed.)

harrow_intro.speaker: narrator
harrow_intro.text: Harrow Landing. Night. Half the windows on Lamp Square are dark.

harrow_intro.speaker: narrator
harrow_intro.text: Red's lamp has burned ten years. Oil costs a meal now. She lights it anyway. Tap the glass twice, then get to work.

harrow_intro.speaker: narrator
harrow_intro.text: (The courier office is next door. Press the button at things to use them.)

harrow_home_again.speaker: narrator
harrow_home_again.text: Home again. The lamp is still on. Across Lamp Square, a few more windows have lit since she left.

harrow_home_again.speaker: narrator
harrow_home_again.text: Red holds the beacon part up to the lamp. Her ears go straight up. Her tail starts wagging on its own.

harrow_ex_tally.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_tally.text: A wall of tally marks. One for every night the lamp has burned.

harrow_ex_photo.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_photo.text: A photo on the shelf. A woman in a flight jacket, waving at whoever took it.

harrow_ex_charts.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_charts.text: Mom's old flight charts, pinned to the wall. Red can't read them. She traces the lines anyway.

harrow_dispatcher_b1.speaker: crowd_dispatcher
harrow_dispatcher_b1.text: You're late. Job's on the board. Watch Zero's crate washed up at Otis's dock, and the Signals are all over it.

harrow_dispatcher_b1.speaker: crowd_dispatcher
harrow_dispatcher_b1.text: Take the job, get a claim slip. And don't touch the stamp.

harrow_dispatcher_b2.speaker: crowd_dispatcher
harrow_dispatcher_b2.text: Crate claimed? Then why are you still standing here? ...Don't tell Kasp I said that.

harrow_dispatcher_b3.speaker: crowd_dispatcher
harrow_dispatcher_b3.text: *STAMP* DONE. I have waited all year to do that.

harrow_store_b1.speaker: crowd_shopkeeper
harrow_store_b1.text: Watch Zero bought every thermos in the shop. Every one. I've got nothing to put coffee in. ...Or any coffee.

harrow_store_b2.speaker: crowd_shopkeeper
harrow_store_b2.text: I heard about the fight. ...Tell me everything. Quietly. Start with the part where he fell.

harrow_store_clerk.speaker: crowd_clerk
harrow_store_clerk.text: Antacids. For nerves. Ticket quota's up again. ...I used to like this town.

harrow_gear_b1.speaker: crowd_welder
harrow_gear_b1.text: That's a sword, kid? That's a butter knife with confidence.

harrow_gear_b2.speaker: crowd_welder
harrow_gear_b2.text: Heard you dented a Signals helmet. ...Quietly, I'm proud. Want a better dent-maker?

harrow_ex_gear_sign.speaker: sign
harrow_ex_gear_sign.text: ASK ABOUT THE WICKED AWESOME. (We don't have it. Ask anyway. Asking is still free.)

harrow_ex_bridge_lamp_alone.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bridge_lamp_alone.text: A rusty ship's bridge lamp sits on Otis's desk.

harrow_ex_bridge_lamp.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bridge_lamp.text: A rusty ship's bridge lamp sits on Otis's desk.

harrow_ex_bridge_lamp.speaker: otis
harrow_ex_bridge_lamp.text: Came off a hull I hauled for the Navy. Somebody'd left it on.

harrow_ex_roster.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_roster.text: A roster board. Every dockhand's name in chalk, in Otis's careful hand.

harrow_ex_coughdrops.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_coughdrops.text: A dented tin of cough drops. One left. Otis is saving it.

harrow_office_chime.speaker: otis
harrow_office_chime.text: Crate's by the door, friend. Take it before Kasp thinks of a form for it.

harrow_bar_keeper_b1.speaker: crowd_bartender
harrow_bar_keeper_b1.text: Tonight's special is an argument. Keep it down, though. Arguments are noise.

harrow_bar_keeper_b2.speaker: crowd_bartender
harrow_bar_keeper_b2.text: First round's on the house. Don't tell the Signals. Or my accountant. ...Actually, tell everyone.

harrow_fly_a_b1.speaker: crowd_barfly_a
harrow_fly_a_b1.text: The Zeroes are camped at the mast. Ringing their bells. On purpose. ...Somebody's bringing them soup.

harrow_fly_a_b2.speaker: crowd_barfly_a
harrow_fly_a_b2.text: Heard Red flattened 'bout ten of 'em. Or eleven. Math's hard.

harrow_fly_b_b1.speaker: crowd_barfly_b
harrow_fly_b_b1.text: My cousin keeps a receiver under her floor. Says the call's louder every night. ...Says it's humming.

harrow_fly_b_b2.speaker: crowd_barfly_b
harrow_fly_b_b2.text: The call's louder since the fight. Coincidence? Probably. I've been drinking.

harrow_fly_c_b1.speaker: crowd_barfly_c
harrow_fly_c_b1.text: I'd tell you a rumor, but the walls here have headphones.

harrow_fly_c_b3.speaker: crowd_barfly_c
harrow_fly_c_b3.text: Fifty troopers. FLATTENED. Don't let anyone tell you forty-nine.

harrow_legend_bar.speaker: crowd_barfly_c
harrow_legend_bar.text: ...and then Red flattened FIFTY troopers! All at once! With a LAMP!

harrow_legend_bar.speaker: narrator
harrow_legend_bar.text: (Red holds up three fingers. Then two more. Then flexes. Somewhere at the bar, somebody laughs out loud. It startles them.)

harrow_legend_bar.speaker: crowd_barfly_c
harrow_legend_bar.text: Five! Even better! Somebody write it down!

harrow_old_dark.speaker: crowd_old_barfly
harrow_old_dark.text: My lamp's out. The window over the store. Spent the oil on bets. Don't tell anyone. ...Everyone knows.

harrow_old_done.speaker: crowd_old_barfly
harrow_old_done.text: Lamp's lit over the store. ...That was you, wasn't it? The Kincaid kid. Quiet thanks, kid.

harrow_ex_bar_bets_b1.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bar_bets_b1.text: THE BETS BOARD. KASP VS ZERO, stakes in rations. RAIN BY MORNING: 50 to 1. Someone has drawn a duck. Nobody owns up.

harrow_ex_bar_bets_b2.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bar_bets_b2.text: THE BETS BOARD, REDRAWN. COURIER AND BEAR: 1 to 1. KASP: 100 to 1. RAIN: 50 to 1.

harrow_ex_bar_bets_b3.speaker: narrator
harrow_ex_bar_bets_b3.text: THE BETS BOARD. Everything is crossed out. One line is new: PAID. Below it, smaller: NEXT BET: SOMETHING BIGGER.
